stories.title: Settlers attack Palestinian olive harvest, injuring farmers, dual nationals and journalist
stories.summary: Dozens of masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian olive farmers in the occupied West Bank during the annual harvest, setting fire to cars and olive trees. The violence injured 12 Palestinians, including four who hold both Palestinian and American citizenship, and a foreign journalist who suffered head and neck injuries; a council member said an American citizen named Majdi was hit with nail‑studded sticks and his elderly mother was also wounded.
stories.why: The incident highlights escalating settler violence that endangers civilians and press freedom in the West Bank.
stories.previousTitle: Masked settlers attack Palestinians and journalist during West Bank olive harvest
stories.previousSummary: Dozens of masked settlers assaulted Palestinians near the village of Abu Falah during the annual olive harvest, setting fire to cars and olive trees. A local official reported 12 Palestinians injured, including four dual Palestinian‑American citizens, and a foreign journalist was also wounded. Witnesses said an American citizen named Majdi was struck with nail‑studded sticks, sustaining deep head injuries, and his elderly mother was also hurt.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: Record number of ship attacks reported in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows that twelve vessels were reported attacked between 5 and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the US‑Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw ten ships reporting attacks, and six vessels were struck on Sunday, a one‑day high. Industry data suggests the rise in incidents has coincided with a slowdown in the recovery of oil shipments through the strait.
stories.why: The surge in attacks threatens the flow of oil through a key global shipping chokepoint.
stories.previousTitle: Record number of ship attacks reported in Strait of Hormuz this week
stories.previousSummary: BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows twelve vessels were reported attacked between 5 and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the US‑Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw ten attacks, including six vessels struck on a single Sunday, a one‑day high, and four attacks reported so far this week. Industry data suggests the rise in incidents has slowed the recent recovery in oil shipments through the strait.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: India's forex reserves drop $60 billion in six weeks as RBI intervenes
stories.summary: Over a six‑week period, India's foreign‑exchange reserves fell by about $60 billion. The Reserve Bank of India bought dollars in the market to support the rupee, which has been one of the weakest Asian currencies this year. The drawdown reflects pressure on the currency and the central bank’s stabilisation effort.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
stories.previousTitle: India's forex reserves shed $60 billion in six weeks as RBI steps in to support rupee, one of Asia's worst-performing currencies this year
stories.previousSummary: India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by nearly $60 billion in six weeks to $726.027 billion as of October 9, from a record high of $785.706 billion on September 4. The fall was largely attributed to the Reserve Bank of India’s intervention to support the rupee amid rising crude oil prices, higher US yields and sustained foreign investor outflows.
stories.change: Material details changed since the previous brief.

stories.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
stories.summary: Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.
stories.previousTitle: Houthi missile strike hits Aden presidential palace, five killed, 16 injured
stories.previousSummary: A Houthi missile attack struck al‑Maashiq Palace, the presidential palace in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16, including site guards and civilian employees. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al‑Eryani said the prime minister and other ministers were unharmed. The Houthis said the strike targeted what they called the “Saudi enemy’s military operations headquarters” in Aden.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.
